cliche: Match cut to the next scene (a label, with no object named)
instead: Name the object that crosses the cut and the frame where both scenes are true: 'the cursor stays at (640, 400) while the sidebar row behind it becomes the page header'.

cliche: The logo assembles from particles
instead: Build the mark from the product's own parts: the UI element that already has the mark's silhouette scales into place and the rest of the screen clears around it.

cliche: Text types on letter by letter as the idea
instead: Type into the real input field only when the typing is the product's real action; otherwise let the line be cut in on a beat or lifted through a mask.

cliche: The phone floats and rotates in a void
instead: Keep the device out. Put the real UI full-bleed, or have the camera pass through the real screen to the next state.

cliche: A glow line sweeps across the text or card
instead: Light the element through its own state change: the selection highlight the product really draws, moving to the next real item.

cliche: The camera pushes into the screen
instead: Push into one named UI element that becomes the next scene's ground (the badge, the row, the send arrow), with a fixed anchor point.

cliche: Zoom-through between any two scenes
instead: Choose the object that scales and what is inside it. A zoom-through needs the thing being entered: the dot of the i, the avatar, the input.

cliche: Fade to black between scenes
instead: Cut on a strong frame, or carry one element across the cut so there is no black.

cliche: Whip pan as a generic energy transition
instead: Whip only along the film's one direction, with the incoming scene's first element already moving at the same speed.

cliche: A light leak or lens flare burn between scenes
instead: Let the next scene's own bright element (a window, a highlight, a white card) flood the frame as the hand-off.

cliche: A glitch or datamosh cut with no glitch concept
instead: Break one specific thing (a row mis-sorts, a number flickers) because the product fixes it, then restore it with the product's own motion.

cliche: Cards float in parallax with no cause
instead: Move layers only when a camera move or a hand reveals depth; each layer must be a real screen the viewer needs.

cliche: Three feature cards slide in one after another
instead: Show each feature as one real interaction in the same window, the output of one the input of the next.

cliche: Glowing orbs, particles or bokeh as atmosphere
instead: Use no atmosphere. Put the 2 px real UI edge, a real shadow and the product's own colours where the atmosphere would have been.

cliche: A blue-purple gradient mesh behind everything
instead: Use the brand's own ground colour or the design system's neutral; spend the colour on one accent that does a job.

cliche: A big stat counts up on a black card, alone
instead: Count the number inside the real UI where it lives, then hand off one digit or the unit to the next element.

cliche: Every element enters with a whoosh and a slide-up
instead: Make most elements simply there on the cut; give exactly one moving thing a motivated entrance and a sound on its contact frame.

cliche: Fade and slide up on every entrance
instead: Pick the entrance by the object's nature: type rises through a line mask, UI scales from the click that spawned it, shapes draw on, hard beats cut in.

cliche: Everything scales in with a bounce overshoot
instead: Settle with one ease family; overshoot only on the one thing that lands with weight.

cliche: A constant-speed orbit around a floating object
instead: Hold the camera still, or move it with a leg that has an anticipation, a peak and a landing, on a reason.

cliche: A 3D shape spinning in a void as a stand-in for the product
instead: Put the real product on a plane in space and move the camera past it; the object in 3D is the real UI.

cliche: The sparkles icon or a glowing brain for AI
instead: Show the AI's real output arriving in the real UI: the streamed answer, the changed diff, the filled field.

cliche: A glowing globe with connecting arcs
instead: Show the real scale as the real thing: the list that is 4 000 rows long, scrolling at the speed the product scrolls it.

cliche: Isometric cards or panels floating at an angle
instead: Place real screens flat and straight, and move the camera, not the panels.

cliche: A dashboard floating at a 30 degree tilt over a gradient
instead: Show the real dashboard straight on, full-bleed, and animate one real value changing.

cliche: A problem montage of stressed people and stock icons
instead: Show the problem as the real broken state in the real UI (the 4-hour-old thread, the red badge, the queue).

cliche: The logo spins or rotates in on the end card
instead: Hold the real logo file still on a clean card, with the end line the largest type; let the previous shot hand off to it.

cliche: Confetti or fireworks on the CTA
instead: Let the last state change of the product be the celebration: the checkmark the product really shows.

cliche: A typewriter headline over a blurred background
instead: Let the headline be set once, large, and cut in on the beat; blur nothing.

cliche: A slow Ken Burns on a still screenshot
instead: Move the real UI: scroll it, click it, stream it. If it must be a still, give it a camera move with a stated anchor.

cliche: Zoom on a screenshot with a circle callout
instead: Use a focus zoom into the actual region, with the camera easing 150 ms behind the cursor.

cliche: A before/after split screen with a sliding divider
instead: Show before and after as one object changing state in place; the change is the transition.

cliche: A 3-2-1 countdown with no stake
instead: Count only a real quantity the product changes (items left, seconds saved) and stop on the real result.

cliche: Testimonial quote cards on soft backgrounds
instead: Show the person's real words as the real UI element they were in (the reply, the review row) and cut straight to them.

cliche: Stock handshakes, high-fives and smiling teams
instead: Show the real collaboration in the product: two cursors, a shared selection, a comment resolving.

cliche: A magic wand, spell or sparkle when the AI does its job
instead: Show the cause and the effect with the same cursor, one frame apart; the speed is the magic.

cliche: A rocket, a ladder or a mountain for growth or success
instead: Show the number moving on the product's real chart, with a sourced figure and a held beat.

cliche: A lightbulb turning on for an idea
instead: Show the idea as the first real keystroke or the first row that appears.

cliche: Text reveals by dissolving from particles or dust
instead: Reveal text through a mask line or by deleting what covers it, in the product's own type.

cliche: A liquid blob morph between two unrelated shapes
instead: Morph between two shapes that share a silhouette and a meaning, with a held legible mid-state.

cliche: Film burn, scratches or grain overlays as texture
instead: Take texture only from the brand's film card. If it is flat, add none.

cliche: A tilted dutch-angle UI for energy
instead: Keep the UI level; get energy from timing, cuts on the beat and one decisive camera move.

cliche: Artificial handheld shake on a UI
instead: Move with deliberate, eased legs. If it needs to feel human, make the cursor hesitate.

cliche: Motion-trail ghost copies on every move
instead: Use real motion blur on the whip frames only; leave everything else clean.

cliche: A pulsing ring around the button the viewer should click
instead: Let the cursor arrive and rest on the button; the rest is the emphasis.

cliche: A blurred infinite scroll of feature text
instead: Scroll the real list at the product's speed and land on the one row the film is about.

cliche: Abstract shapes floating in at the start for no reason
instead: Open on the real UI's first state, or on the one shape the brand mark is made of.
